findings.title: fill_in_legal.py exits 0 without applying a value that was changed after a fill; the data file and the published text then disagree
findings.evidence: probe_fill2.txt (temp copies, adv-a sample_043_gcc_b): ran a full fill (rc0), then changed one value and re-ran. SUPPORT_EMAIL, PRIVACY_EMAIL, WITHDRAW_PATH, GOVERNING_LAW, minors_clause and inapp_notif_clause each gave rc=0, no output and 0 files changed, and the new value appears in no document. The cause: _substitute (scripts/fill_in_legal.py:212) only replaces <PLACEHOLDER:X> tokens, and those are gone after the first fill. Values inside a fork variant (CONTROLLER_NAME, POSTAL_ADDRESS, trade_name) fail loudly instead, with rc3 and the misleading message 'fork d5_identity (ar, privacy): expected exactly one variant in the text, found none'. Nothing in the suite compares the data-file values with the documents: T2 checks only that no tokens remain. Realistic path: the native AR review (a UL3 merge gate) corrects WITHDRAW_PATH_AR or GOVERNING_LAW_AR after the fill-in, the orchestrator re-runs, gets rc0, and the unreviewed wording ships while the data file records the reviewed one. GREEN-EN's stated limit covers only derived clauses, not plain placeholders.
findings.fix: Add a post-condition in plan() after filling. Every placeholder key with a non-empty value must appear in at least one filled output document (an AR document for keys ending in _AR). Otherwise raise FillInError: '<KEY>: value not in the documents (already filled? restore the pre-fill markdown from git, or set it null if no selected variant uses it)'. Measured as feasible: after a normal fill, all 16 non-empty sample values are present (probe_postcheck). Give the 'found none' fork error the same hint.

findings.title: The fill-in writes the six markdown files and only then finds that a landing page cannot be rendered
findings.evidence: probe_fill.txt P3: landing/support.html without its end marker. run() (fill_in_legal.py:344-349) writes all six .md files ('wrote: ...'). renderer.write_regions then raises LegalRenderError. main() catches only FillInError (:365), so the run ends with a traceback, rc 1, filled markdown and stale pages. This contradicts the docstring ('It writes NOTHING while ... any document or variant is inconsistent'). A locked file part-way through the write loop leaves a similar mixed state. T5 and T2 turn red on the result and a re-run heals it, so the defect is recoverable.
findings.fix: Before the first write_bytes in run(), check each page: for page in renderer.SOURCES: renderer._split_page((repo_root/page).read_bytes().decode('utf-8'), page). In main, catch (FillInError, renderer.LegalRenderError), or load the renderer first and catch its error class.

T5 compares the committed regions with the same renderer's output and probes only text escaping. The documents contain no links today, but *_COUNSEL values may contain [ ] ( ) (_FORBIDDEN_IN_COUNSEL_VALUE allows them). The current behaviour is correct (probe_render.txt: javascript:/data:/quote/< hrefs render as escaped literal text; idempotent; chrome bytes equal; 0/2 marker pairs raise); it is just unpinned.

(a) render_markdown('[x](javascript:alert(1)) [y](https://a.example/?a=1&b=2)') contains no 'href="javascript' and does contain 'href="https://a.example/?a=1&b=2"'. (b) write_regions on a tmp copy of the six pages and sources: a second call returns [], bytes outside the region are unchanged, and a CRLF page has no bare LF. findings.title: No test in the suite runs scripts/fill_in_legal.py, the tool that will produce the publication commit
findings.evidence: PM09 (writes despite missing answers), PM10 (_check_value disabled) and PM11 (bool fork key inverted) all SURVIVED, with T2 as the only red. GREEN-EN's 31-check fillin_check.py lives in the scratchpad, not in the repo. The post-fill checks (T2, T5, T8, T11) catch some wrong outputs but not wrong values (see B1).
findings.fix: Commit a tmp-copy test of the fill-in. It should cover: all-null gives rc 2 and writes nothing; synthetic complete answers give rc 0, no PLACEHOLDER, first dates unchanged and a second run that changes nothing; a value with markup or a token gives rc 3; flipping d3 changes the fork text. Add the B1 post-condition case once it exists.

findings.title: An empty string is refused for a value only an unselected variant uses, with a false message
findings.evidence: probe_fill.txt P13: CR_NUMBER '' with d5=A, and LEGAL_BASIS_COUNSEL(_AR) / TRANSFER_BASIS_COUNSEL(_AR) '' with counsel_review=false, give rc3 '<KEY> is empty but the documents use it'. null is accepted (P13b). The cause: _apply_fork computes the filled form of every variant through _filled -> _substitute (:228-229), which raises for '' even when the variant is not selected. The fixture comment invites '' ('CR_NUMBER (d5 B only)', 'counsel ... needed only when counsel_review is true'). A10's AR counsel refusal reaches the user through the same path.
findings.fix: In _filled (fill_in_legal.py:233), catch FillInError and return None: a variant whose values cannot be filled cannot be the one in the text. Validation of the selected text stays in fill().

findings.title: The renderer silently mis-renders markdown outside its subset; counsel values may introduce such markdown, and the App renders it differently
findings.evidence:
probe_render.txt: 'Intro\n1. first\n2. second' becomes one

; a nested ' - b' is flattened into a sibling item; a continuation line after an item is split off as a separate

; '**see [x](u) now**' keeps literal '**'; '## C# and F#' renders as 'C# and F'; a UTF-8 BOM turns the h1 into a

(_read_source uses utf-8, not utf-8-sig); '**a *b** c*' produces mis-nested strong/em. LegalScreen's markdown-it (react-native-markdown-display, typographer true) renders these as lists, so the web and App versions diverge. None of these constructs is in the six sources today (scan_md.txt: 0 hits). *_COUNSEL values may span lines and use markdown (fill_in_legal.py:77), and T5 cannot detect the problem because it compares the renderer with itself. There is no escaping impact: only / are ever inserted.
findings.fix: Make _blocks (render_legal_landing.py:110) raise LegalRenderError on a line outside the subset: numbered or star/plus bullets, an indented '- ', '>', a '|' row, '#{4,}', a horizontal rule, or a non-item line directly after an item. Read sources with utf-8-sig. Alternatively, reject those patterns in _check_value for counsel keys.

findings.title: render_legal_landing --check prints a traceback on a missing page
findings.evidence: probe_render.txt: stale_regions (render_legal_landing.py:259) calls read_bytes on a missing page, which raises FileNotFoundError, not LegalRenderError, so main() (:281) does not catch it and --check does not exit 2.
findings.fix: In stale_regions, before reading: if not (repo_root / page).is_file(): raise LegalRenderError(f'page missing: {page}').

findings.title: LegalScreen keeps the previous language's document when a language-change refetch fails
findings.evidence: load() (LegalScreen.tsx:67-87) never clears content. When lang changes, the fetch fails and the new language has no cache, errorKey is set but hidden (the error block needs !content), so the other language's text stays on screen with no banner. Reasoned from the code, not measured. In practice it is hard to reach: language is changed on Profile, and Legal is popped first.
findings.fix: Optional: setContent(null) at the start of load when lang differs from the last loaded language, or render the screen with key={lang}.

findings.title: Deploy order: the backend must serve ?lang before the OTA ships
findings.evidence: An older backend ignores the unknown lang query parameter (FastAPI) and returns English. A new client then caches that English (or a DRAFT, if served) under legal_cache_{doc}_ar. Online fetches self-heal; only offline views are affected.
findings.fix: In the PR body: deploy the backend (Railway) before or together with the EAS update.

summary:
Engineering verdict on U8 GREEN: DEFECTIVE. I found one major defect and no blocking one of my own. Adversary A's blocking A1 stands: I confirmed the code facts behind it.

**Major (B1).** Re-running scripts/fill_in_legal.py after a fill with a corrected value returns 0 and changes nothing. This holds for the emails, WITHDRAW_PATH, GOVERNING_LAW and the derived booleans. Values inside a fork variant fail with a misleading 'found none' instead. Nothing cross-checks the data file against the documents, so a value corrected by the AR native review could ship unapplied. A value-presence post-condition fixes it; I measured it as feasible on a normal fill.

**Minors.**
- B2: a renderer error after the markdown writes leaves the markdown filled and the pages stale, with an uncaught LegalRenderError.
- B3 and B4: the renderer's link safety and write path, and the whole fill-in script, have no test in the suite.
- B5: an empty string for a value only an unselected variant uses is refused, with a false message.
- B6: markdown outside the renderer's subset (numbered lines, nested items, continuation lines, BOM) is mis-rendered without an error. Counsel values may bring it in; none is in today's sources.

**Notes:** B7-B11.

**What held up:**
- Renderer: no escaping hole; idempotent; chrome unchanged outside the region; 0 or 2 marker pairs refused.
- Fill-in: refuses every null and every invalid value, never moves the date anchors, and a second run is stable.
- Route: 24 hostile lang values reach only the four legal filenames.
- Client: per-language cache keys are isolated and the pre-U8 key is never read.
- Gates: comm gate with comm -13 empty (1628 = 1628); OpenAPI pins 141 passed; full jest 3533 passed; tsc and eslint clean; no secret-shaped literals.

**Mutants (25 own):** 14 killed, 11 survived. Survivors: PM01, PM02, PM05, PM06, PM07, PM09, PM10, PM11, PM12, CM04, CM08; each survivor's finding names the node to add.
